solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greedy one studies food supply – his targets were sounder, but loose?

definitions.text: his targets were sounder, but loose?
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the official it describes

blocks.note: a greedy person is a hog
to con is to study or learn by heart
the table is the food provided, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A glutton reads up on food provision, followed by a riddling aside about a man whose quarry was sounder yet loose.
explanation.walkthrough: A sounder is a herd of wild pigs, so 'sounder, but loose' means pigs running free; 'sounder' poses as a comparative of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog-constable was a parish official whose job was rounding up stray swine, the loose members of a sounder.

clue.text: Rash that's gone is characterized by ditty wet composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: if a thing is characterized by a quality, it has it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song considered feeble and wet is described as hasty in composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's gone' belongs to the definition: it marks the word as obsolete, as Chambers does.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty-witted is an obsolete compound meaning rash or acting without thought.

clue.text: Staffage appalling at Balmoral in queen being put up therein

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, means raised so the letters read bottom to top
therein means inside that, so these pieces are placed within the other

blocks.note: gash is Scots for ghastly; Balmoral is the royal estate in Scotland
taken as written
R, regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Dreadful decorations at the royal Scottish castle with the Queen staying there.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral Castle is in Aberdeenshire, so 'at Balmoral' asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffage is the decorative extras added to a painting or design, which is garnish or embellishment.

clue.text: Crows with recipe taking second place in 'Bake-off' submissions?

indicators.note: taking second place in means slotting in at position two of the other word

blocks.note: contestants on the baking show The Great British Bake Off submit cakes
R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone crowing as their recipe comes second in a television baking contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a popular UK television baking competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crake is to utter a harsh cry like a crow, so crakes is a verb meaning crows.

clue.text: Where chalk's applied at the right moment (5, two words)

blocks.note: first meaning: a snooker player chalks the tip of the stick
second meaning: exactly when signalled, as an actor enters

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: chalk goes on the stick used in snooker and pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely on time, like a performer entering on a prompt; literally it is the location of chalk on a billiard stick.

clue.text: Some turning up seeking famed Louvre piece head off

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the next word
turning up in a down clue means flipping so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: a run of letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Visitors turning up to the Louvre to look for a famous exhibit missing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' is part of the definition, not a deletion: the statue has no head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winged Victory of Samothrace, a headless statue of the goddess Nike, is one of the Louvre's most famous works.

clue.text: Part of knight's foot armour, forged o' steel, left and right

indicators.note: forged means hammered into shape, so the letters are beaten into a new form

blocks.note: o' is the clipped of, giving its letter
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A knight's armour for the foot, hammered from steel to fit both left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A solleret is the jointed steel shoe of a suit of armour, protecting the foot.

clue.text: Unusual lamp, grand when planted in a border

indicators.note: planted in means set into the ground, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: a rand is a border or strip, as of leather on a shoe
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An odd lamp looks splendid when set in a flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' poses as an adjective, but it is a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argand is an oil lamp with a tubular wick, invented by Aimé Argand, an unusual design in its day.

clue.text: Heap of refuse, last to be cast from furnace's function?

indicators.note: cast from means thrown out of, so some letters are removed

blocks.note: a blast furnace works by blasting air through it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Waste piled up, the final residue cast out of a furnace's workings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like a selection signal for a final letter, but the whole word is what gets removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bing is a northern and Scots word for a heap, especially a spoil heap of mine waste.

clue.text: Iron tenon: some instruction required with one installed

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside, so these pieces are placed within the other

blocks.note: a lesson is a piece of instruction
W is the abbreviation for with
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fitting an iron joint requires a little instruction and one part put in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lewisson, or lewis, is an iron dovetail tenon fitted into a stone block so it can be lifted.

clue.text: The old caution a nation initially welcoming conflict …

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only of the word it follows
welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
war is armed conflict
the first letter of nation

explanation.surface: An old warning that a country is about to welcome hostilities, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word, here a verb form of warn with the old prefix a-; the ellipsis links the surface to 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarn is an obsolete verb meaning to warn, so it is caution as a verb in older English.

clue.text: … Those engaged losing millions – it's a sign

indicators.note: losing something means it is no longer there, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: armies are those engaged in the conflict of the previous clue
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Continuing the war story: the combatants have lost millions, an ominous sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'conflict' over from 10-across, so 'those engaged' are fighters in that war.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Product of teashop creator … OAP's thrilled with it!

definitions.text: Product of teashop creator … OAP's thrilled with it!

indicators.note: thrilled means excited and stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: the full set of letters, which the anagram must yield
letters that join the answer in the anagram, to be taken away

explanation.surface: A pensioner delighted by a cake made by the creator of a tea room.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus OAP rearranges to TEASHOP CREATOR. OAP, old-age pensioner, is the British term for a senior citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachertorte is the Viennese chocolate cake devised by Franz Sacher, whose family founded the Hotel Sacher café.

clue.text: Join climbers in Cairngorms? Retreating, deer whines

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the following words are read from the end

blocks.note: an elk is a large deer
to carp is to complain or whine

explanation.surface: An invitation to go climbing in the Scottish Cairngorms, while a retreating deer complains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cairngorms are Scottish mountains; the question mark signals that the answer is a Scots word for what climbers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprackle is a Scots verb meaning to clamber, which is what someone joining climbers in the Scottish hills would do.

clue.text: Eastern prince, reverse of British noodle?

indicators.note: the reverse of something is it read from the other end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
noodle and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A Malay prince is pictured as the opposite of a silly British head.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunku is a title given to a prince in Malaysia, a ruler in the East.

clue.text: Melting glacier shifting right to left – sort of nutty?

indicators.note: shifting one thing to another means swapping it, so one letter is exchanged for the other
melting loses its form, so the letters flow into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A glacier melts and moves, and someone wonders if it is a bit nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R in the glacier for an L, then rearrange. 'Nutty' is not 'mad' but literal: the word relates to nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellagic means derived from gallnuts, as in ellagic acid, so it is nutty in a botanical sense.

clue.text: Satisfied sound, once, about effort of scrum in easy win

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: pur is an old spelling of purr, a contented sound
a rugby scrum is a pushing contest, a shove

explanation.surface: A purr of contentment after the scrum's effort produces a comfortable victory.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum in rugby is where the two packs push against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is a contest or task easily won, something offering no resistance.

clue.text: Old peasant troubled shrink admitting start of eccentricity

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so these letters are stirred into another order
the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept here
admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of eccentricity

explanation.surface: A rustic of olden days, troubled, sees a psychiatrist who takes in his oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist in the surface but is just the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kernish is an obsolete word from kern, an Irish foot soldier or rustic, so it denotes a peasant of former times.

clue.text: Render in rough stone old-style wharf, possibly first installed

indicators.note: possibly marks one of many arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged
installed means fitted within, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: kay is an old spelling of quay, a wharf
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old wharf being turned into rough stonework, with something laid in first.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is not in the dictionaries, so Azed defines it himself from karst, the rough limestone terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Karst is rugged, eroded limestone landscape, so to karstify is to turn rock into that rough stony form.

clue.text: Cheeky minx, woman replacing husband, mimsy one

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped in for another

blocks.note: a hussy is a cheeky or brazen girl
W is the abbreviation for woman
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A saucy girl has a woman stand in for her husband, then a prim figure appears.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimsy, from Lewis Carroll, means prim or feeble, the opposite of the cheeky minx in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A wussy is a feeble, timid person, a weakling, which suits someone mimsy.

clue.text: Coarse Scots when going after Mrs Grundy, firing off extremes

indicators.note: firing off the extremes means shooting away both end letters
going after means placed behind, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: Mrs Grundy is the proverbial narrow-minded prude
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Rough Scotsmen behave crudely around the prim Mrs Grundy, sending her running.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy is a character from an 18th-century play who became a byword for prudishness. 'Scots' labels the answer as a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudas is a Scots adjective meaning coarse or rough-mannered, especially of an old woman.

clue.text: Nurse comes round opening up premed alkaline

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the alkaloid, a noun

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
coming round something means surrounding it, so that piece goes inside

blocks.note: aia, or ayah, is a nurse or nanny in India
a port is an opening, as in a porthole

explanation.surface: A nurse comes round after a patient's premedication, opening up the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes round' reads like waking from anaesthetic, which fits the premed surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropia is another name for atropine, an alkaloid given as a premedication to dry secretions before surgery.

clue.text: Like a debutante presented to Her Majesty in very fine fabric? Quite

blocks.note: a debutante is a young woman, a she
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A debutante being presented at court to the Queen, wearing a filmy gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: she presented to ER, a fine fabric, and quite. Debutantes were once formally presented to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means diaphanous when used of fabric, and as an adverb it means utterly or quite.

clue.text: Prophet's descendants rising proudly to the surface, last rising about halfway

indicators.note: last rising about halfway means the final letter climbs to near the middle, reordering the word

blocks.note: emerse is a botanical term for leaves standing up out of the water

explanation.surface: The Prophet's line rises proudly into view.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the last letter is at the bottom, so it rises to the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeer is a variant of emir, a title borne by descendants of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Is this player, shiner, exciting in orchestra?

indicators.note: exciting stirs things up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: the full set of letters, which the anagram must yield
letters that join the answer in the anagram, to be taken away

explanation.surface: Asks whether a star performer would be thrilling playing in an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: 'this' stands for the answer, and this plus SHINER rearranges to IN ORCHESTRA, so remove SHINER from those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a performer on stage, so a player in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Critic having to push off, disowned by leader

indicators.note: disowned by its leader means the front letter abandons the word

blocks.note: to scarper is British slang for to run away, push off

explanation.surface: A critic forced to leave after being disowned by his chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A carper is someone who finds fault, a nagging critic.

clue.text: Disciple of theological pioneer admitting 50% of errors

indicators.note: 50% is half, so half of the word is kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: tho', short for though, means admitting that
mistakes are errors

explanation.surface: A follower of an early theologian concedes that half of what he wrote was wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' looks like a containment signal but is the word though, in its shortened poetic spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thomist follows Thomas Aquinas, the medieval pioneer of systematic theology.

clue.text: Prepare for solids? Och aye, mashed neaps

indicators.note: mashed means crushed to a pulp, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written, though it sounds like neeps, Scots turnips

explanation.surface: A Scottish parent weaning a baby on mashed turnip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Och aye' tags the answer as Scots. Neeps, Scots for turnips, are traditionally mashed, though the fodder is spelt neaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Spane is Scots for wean, getting a baby off milk and ready for solid food.

clue.text: Downy plant coverings: chaps installed full amount almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off
installed means put in place inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: chaps are men
a total is the full amount

explanation.surface: Men fitting fuzzy covers onto plants, having nearly used up the whole supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomenta, plural of tomentum, are the matted woolly hairs that coat some leaves and stems.

clue.text: What kept Pyramus from Thisbe – or Ida from mice!

indicators.note: one thing from another means taking it away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: Muridae is the zoological family of mice and rats
taken as written

explanation.surface: Contrasts the lovers' famous barrier with a woman named Ida kept away from mice.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Pyramus and Thisbe story, as staged in A Midsummer Night's Dream, the lovers are parted by a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mure is an archaic word for a wall, the barrier through which Pyramus and Thisbe whispered.

clue.text: Passage in Iliad italicized

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A passage of Homer's epic printed in italics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a piece of text in the Iliad; it is a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine, so a passage underground.

clue.text: Militant supporting what's left of spread

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
VO, verso, is the left-hand page of an open book's spread

explanation.surface: A militant backs whatever is left of a spread, perhaps a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests food, but it is a two-page spread in a book, whose left page is the verso.
explanation.definitionFit: A Provo was a member of the Provisional IRA, a militant republican group.

clue.text: I'll be captivated by s-spiffy little bird on the river

indicators.note: being captivated by something means being held captive inside it

blocks.note: spiffy means dapper, and the stammered s- asks for the first letter doubled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stammering that they will be charmed by a smart little waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in s-spiffy tells you to stutter the synonym too, repeating its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A didapper is a dabchick or little grebe, a small diving bird found on rivers and ponds.

clue.text: Place giving Aussie bad feeling? Leaving capital optional

blocks.note: first meaning: the city in Northern Ireland
second meaning: Australian slang for a grudge or dislike
a pointer to the first meaning: the city's full name begins with London, the capital, which may be dropped

explanation.surface: Asks which location would leave an Australian feeling sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving capital optional' explains the place: the city is officially Londonderry, and dropping London, the capital, is optional and common.
explanation.definitionFit: Derry is the everyday name for Londonderry, and in Australia to have a derry on someone is to bear a grudge.

clue.text: Catch when fishing round island that's closest for some

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes about the other

blocks.note: a net is the catch-all used when fishing, and to net is to catch
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An angler casts about an island, the nearest one to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For some' marks a dialect word: some speakers say it for nighest.
explanation.definitionFit: Neist is a Scots and northern dialect form of nighest, meaning nearest or next.

clue.text: Erring, betray S. Peter in office of religious elders

indicators.note: erring means going astray, so the letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the abbreviation S. for saint included

explanation.surface: Evokes the apostle betrayed, set inside a church body of elders.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyterate is the office of a presbyter or a body of presbyters, church elders.
